description: Semantic contract edges for the impact proof-cone selector (developer-velocity epic V4a). Production paths declare the contracts they own; tests declare the contracts they exercise. Changing a contract-owning path selects every test claiming that contract. Unknown or undeclared contracts fail closed. This manifest is EXPLICIT and hand-curated; static dependency and coverage relationships are generated and live elsewhere. Every owner/test path must exist in the tree (directory prefix or file); dead edges are a contract defect.

wit-world-interface.description: The WIT world/component interface shape; every WASM service consumer depends on it.

message-envelope.description: Inter-node message envelope/codec and transport contract.

partition-topology.description: Partition topology, split/merge, and placement contracts.

replica-operation-state.description: Replica-operation state machine and terminal-CAS contract.

sql-grammar.description: SQL grammar and statement parser contract.

seed-registration-election-scheduling.description: Seed registration's direct-write leader dependency cut and the partition election scheduler share one transferred leadership gate.

quest-solver-ledger.description: Solver event log, Quest store, and landing/verification contract.

priority-spread-planner-admission.description: Priority spread-cure retention and coordinator admission remain mutually compatible.

priority-services-publication-census.description: Priority SERVICES-row publication supplies every field required by the membership census.

priority-services-marker-reconcile.description: Local-only SERVICES-row marker clearing and reconciliation converge as one retry contract.

replica-durable-generation-cleanup.description: Exact durable replica generations, SERVICES-key cleanup ownership, storage deletion, startup admission, and live-row creation form one lifecycle closure contract.

failed-create-target-authoritative-clean.description: OperationWorkflowOwner alone admits failed create terminalization and cleanup from an exact authoritative lifecycle generation, persists that decision through ReplicaOperationRepository, and re-drives lifecycle-owner release without accepting cache projection as authority.

critical-create-admission-topology-order.description: Critical create admission runs before the downstream topology guard on createOperation.

readiness-versioned-planning-liveness.description: Node-liveness semantic projection, complete-token readiness freshness, macrotask-bounded planning, and non-recursive readiness-internal owner reads form one convergence contract.

active-gate-convergence.description: The canonical active-gate system contract: the control-plane read gateway derives complete-table evidence only from a serving-leader witness, authoritative discovery repair pressure containment and startup ACTIVE convergence stay compatible, the membership-publication owner remains re-entrant and follows live write leadership across fail-back, callers cannot bypass failed-repair backoff, and stale deferred evidence cannot become a permanent ACTIVE veto after newer owner evidence exists.

admin-cache-owner-lifecycle.description: The Admin WebSocket notification subscription and its cache-bound snapshot and repair children transition one coherent read/mutation cache owner pair: same-owner binding is idempotent, handoff generation-fences in-flight and reusable state, and serialized shutdown/restart cannot strand or resurrect a listener.

operation-ledger-self-move-interlock.description: The operation-ledger self-move interlock: hold registration at createOperation, engagement at the dispatching owner's PENDING -> SENDING claim (a foreign holder resolved through the authoritative lifecycle read), and release only by the holder's own terminal row stay one owner contract across the hold policy, the hold state, the admission lanes and the dispatch gate.

formation-release-handoff.description: The seed-owned formation-release handoff: the seed captures, retains and revokes a JOINING cohort generation and publishes a durable release contract; joiners consume it through a typed CONSUMER validation role and release their formation barrier from the whole-plane authority answer, never minting release authority, so the seed authority, the contract/evidence/publication projection and the joiner consumer barrier stay one owner contract.

raft-formation-attribution.description: Formation diagnostics owns the semantic mapping of consensus protocol work to raft_protocol and committed-apply work to raft_apply; the mapping is exclusive, restores callers, and is backend-neutral.

sql-engine-system-table-read.description: System-table reads answered by the SQL engine reflect rows written through the CDC owner; the engine is real on a production-booted node and a contract-bound seam in the membership-consistency harness.

CL-041.description: A follower grants its vote to at most one candidate per term, so at most one leader can be elected per term (Raft §5.2 Election Safety).

CL-040.description: A committed Raft log entry is identical cluster-wide at its index; a follower never stale-commits its own same-index/different-term entry on catch-up (Raft §5.3 Log Matching).

CL-042.description: An empty raft log's last-log-term is 0 (Raft §5.4.1): the consensus core never masquerades an empty log as up-to-date, so a voter holding committed entries denies an empty-log candidate regardless of the candidate's election term (CL-042).

CL-038.description: A surplus-drain REPLACE whose declared source replica is already removed terminalizes (reaches SAFE) instead of re-dispatching a source-leader handoff to a replica that no longer exists (CL-038).

CL-035.description: A replica's committed learner-to-voter raft promotion is seeded into its own node's local SERVICES row at voter-ready activation, so the REPLACE remove-safety gate observes the promotion instead of deferring on a stale learner/null raft_role forever (CL-035).

CL-033.description: The priority-recovery planning projection is memoized per publisher node (build once, reuse while the source revision and stale-grace window hold), so the post-restart recovery hot path cannot rebuild the heavy projection per call and freeze the control-plane seed's event loop past the raft election timeout (CL-033).

CL-034.description: The stage-3 membership-publication planning-snapshot merge (the residual readiness-build cost CL-033's projection memo does not cover) is memoized per publisher node under the same planning-source revision discipline, so per-routing-call rebuild storms cannot freeze the control-plane seed's event loop past the raft election timeout during recovery (CL-034).

CL-001.description: The strict-mode active-node projection retains an already-published node that is transport-alive and within the heartbeat grace through a transient heartbeat-stall trough, while never promoting a non-baseline node on that grace and still trimming a published node that is genuinely stale (CL-001 variant C).

golden-capability-gold-plating.description: A failed or unavailable authoritative read never concludes the positive premise of a safety gate: admission gates fail closed into a typed defer/deny (the conflict-lane deferred-visibility throw; the topology guard's replica_inventory_unusable denial; the surplus REMOVE commit fence; the ledger quorum-spread confirmation). A hold may fail OPEN on a read gap only where blocking on the gap would itself deadlock convergence, and each fail-open hold names its deadlock witness: the over-target count-keyed create-lane hold (G1; fail-closing it would strand the surplus drain it exists to release) and the routine-direction ledger self-move serialization (a disruptive IDLE_ONLY self-move still fails closed). Advisory probes fail open only where a fail-closed enforcer remains downstream (the provisioning ledger-interlock probe defers to operation creation as the enforcing seam).

publication-readiness-churn-liveness-clo.description: After semantic-input quiescence the final complete token is published; during continuous churn completed tokens advance monotonically, dirty owners receive bounded round-robin service, and stale evidence never promotes readiness. Continuous readiness source churn starts at most one heavy planning build globally per macrotask turn and permits a timer or heartbeat sentinel between every pair of heavy items.

architecture-model-chain.description: Executable architecture models are checks: an Alloy assertion, a decision-table rule or an owner-trace violation named by an invariant is validated and run by the model:contracts chain (the ci run's health steps on every main push) and by these tests locally, so a model or registry edit selects the chain.

readiness-handoff-liveness.description: Startup readiness is a controller handoff: the seed registers ready only after its canonical system leaders are in its cache AND its query/data-plane transport is serviceable, and a deferred handoff terminates (ready or blocked with a typed wake) within the bound the owner reports.

core-system-logic.description: The runtime invariants the core-system-logic contract cites (its architecture invariants bind through the Alloy, decision-table and owner-trace checks instead): a stale projection promotes no readiness lane, degraded runtime authority explains but never projects a node, and the seed phase owner transfers the control-plane writers to the steady-state owners on completion.

rolling-restart-rebalancer-handoff.description: The operation-workflow owner bounds deferred re-entry of a coordinator-created remote handoff per operation: retries re-arm with at least the minimum backoff and stop, clearing the retry, once the step has timed out and the operation budget (createdAt + REBALANCE_OPERATION_BUDGET_MS) has passed. Per operation only; the cross-operation cycle is formation-sim's question.

raft-rs-runtime-lifecycle-entry.description: The replica lifecycle owner admits each semantic operation before the runtime owner can enter the raft-rs core, and durable retirement waits for admitted operations before becoming terminal.

raft-rs-runtime-application-transaction.description: Ready processing and the application transaction owner keep application effects, partition progress, raft-rs applied progress, ConfState and each statement's durable outcome coherent across host failure and reconstruction; failure scope follows failure class (a core failure replaces the runtime and resumes every group once, a host failure reconstructs its own group and touches no other group; a failure within one retry window of the last instant the previous one held the group is the same persisting failure, whatever its class and whether or not a reconstruction succeeded in between, so the group is reconstructed at most once per window while it persists - at most ceil(span / window) + 1 reconstructions over any span - and a failure more than one window after the last one starts afresh; a group healed inside a window serves again only after it, so its first write after a heal waits up to one window), a durable record that cannot be read where a group is opened or reconstructed (a missing table, SQLITE_IOERR, SQLITE_CORRUPT) is that group's own typed host failure of phase durable-record-read and never a throw, a record that lost a table is never recreated empty (the record's tables are created in one transaction of the store's own, whole or not at all, so a partial schema only ever comes from outside), a replica whose record cannot be read at open is refused at initialization, typed and naming the phase and the table, whatever its replica count (healing in place is for a group that fails while it runs), a throw the runtime did not type is contained by the port as the group's typed host failure, a group without a usable host announces no role so its partition does not lead, a reconstructed sole voter leads again, a retry is answered from its durable outcome, and the admission owner refuses before consensus (and before a session stages it) every command the application would refuse or never answer.

partition-raft-operation-port.description: The raft-rs runtime is the partition's only consensus backend: PartitionService builds its operation-only port through the fixed raft-rs operation-port owner (no selection and no alternate runtime injection) and consumes semantic operations, typed outcomes and immutable snapshots without a live node/control graph; a refused campaign or peer admission is the port's typed answer, never reported as done; every write the replica did not take is answered by the write kernel's builders, typed with its entry: a pending write released when its replica stops leading, at its commit deadline or at shutdown with what the replica knows of it (outcome unknown once handed to consensus; not leader, deadline passed or service shut down otherwise), a proposal queue at capacity as backpressure with the queue's retry time, a proposal the port refused with the port's reason, and a router holding the answer routes it again by its code (an unknown outcome only under its own entryId); a group held on a contained unexpected throw is named once in the partition's log at error level with its message, and its end once at info.

partition-session-transaction-persistenc.description: A user session's SQLite transaction and the rs-raft store share the partition's one connection: the transaction owner ends its session (COMMIT or ROLLBACK) before it proposes a transaction marker and proposes none while staging; the store refuses every durable consensus write inside a transaction it did not open; the runtime asks that admission before it enters the core and before every Ready, and the write path turns the refusal into a bounded deferral, so no consensus row is ever written inside, or erased by, a user session.

spread-cure-transition-authorization.description: The cure policy owner mints one exact-transition spread-cure authorization; the receiving learner decodes and states exactly that record.

partition-write-answer-retry-classificat.description: The partition write kernel (the answer's code) and the errors owner (its text) are the one owner of what may be done again with a write the partition did not take, and every consumer asks them, never a text of its own: the control plane's retry classification retries every answer but a host failure while proposing (a write whose outcome is unknown did not fail, so it is never recorded as a failed write) - by the kernel's code when it holds the answer, by the errors owner's texts when only a text reached it; a router that sends the write again without its entryId never does so for an unknown outcome - never by its text, and by its code only when it re-proposes under the write's own entryId, where the retry is idempotent.

committed-bootstrap-stamp.description: Every join bootstrap is one canonical own-data stamp read from the group leader before operation persistence, carried unchanged through creation, decoded at the target, and enforced by the raft-rs participation gate; rows remain discovery only and an unreadable or malformed distributed answer fails closed.

replace-owner-membership-observation.description: The REPLACE owner decides source removal, completion and its leadership handoff only from decoded replica consensus observations. The target is a wake and route; the deciding answer must be the leader's own applied-at-commit configuration and a majority of that configuration must corroborate its term and leader identity. The operation port announces applied membership, the partition and node layers relay it, and READ_REPLICA_MEMBERSHIP / RETIRE_REPLICA_PEER read or mutate through the port. Rows never decide membership.

public-application-database-seam.description: The public Application Database seam (createEmbeddedLagrange -> openApplicationDatabase -> query/transaction): public result shape, typed errors, statement policy, and behaviour through embedded processes.

test-listener-port-block.description: A runtime's test listener ports are one allocator block whose admin and transport ports the listener-port model derives from the REST port (getTestListenerPorts); changing the allocator or the port model must re-run the block witness.

public-seam-durability-certification-sou.description: The fixed rs-raft partition construction path makes the provider-neutral public-seam durability scenario eligible as CANDIDATE; the scenario must not consult the retired provider-selection compatibility surface.

harness-docker-build-context.description: The distributed-harness image build context is derived from the Dockerfile's COPY sources; changing either must re-run the parity falsifier.

public-call-outcome-class.description: The call routing contract is the one owner of the public outcome class of a failed CALL (derived from its classification, the per-dispatch invoked flag and the invocation-level execution evidence the call invoker records); the lifecycle command owner's failure projection is the one place that class, retrySafe and the topology-free message reach the PostgreSQL wire, and the public seam proof observes them through a real pg client.

public-binding-two-partition-policy-shap.description: The public Binding fanout proof persists its exact table policy through TablePolicyService, and the production split/merge manager consumes that policy with live child metrics before the harness relies on two frozen partition identities.

partition-replication-start-authorizatio.description: Durable split or merge workflow records authorize exact source START identities; sender delivery classification and PartitionService execution handles preserve that authorization through physical execution.

storage-reservation-authoritative-adopti.description: The reservation lifecycle uses the deterministic operation-derived identity, write-if-absent insertion, and exact authoritative live operation plus ACTIVE reservation witnesses to converge a lost INSERT answer on one durable capacity hold without duplicating creation observations; temporary operation-authority loss retains that hold and one canonical owner retry which survives restart and remains gated before dispatch.

seed-registration-election-scheduling.description: Registration owns the exact direct-write dependency cut and one wait budget; partition scheduling prioritizes that cut and releases all other elections without restating it.

priority-spread-planner-retention-admiss.description: The planner must retain the same over-target spread cure that coordinator admission permits.

priority-services-row-publication-census.description: Published priority SERVICES rows must satisfy the census field and readiness vocabulary.

priority-services-marker-reconcile.description: The durable-apply marker decision and retry reconciliation must preserve eventual SERVICES-row publication.

replica-durable-generation-cleanup.description: Lifecycle CAS, cleanup-key arbitration, physical storage deletion, and every storage-open admission must preserve one exact durable owner for a logical replica identity.

failed-create-target-authoritative-clean.description: OperationWorkflowOwner terminal admission and repair must carry the exact lifecycle generation through repository persistence and ReplicaHandler cleanup, while projections remain non-authoritative.

critical-create-hold-topology-guard-orde.description: Critical create admission must run before downstream topology checks consume its safety premise.

readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound.description: The readiness owner may reflect every final semantic token only through a globally macrotask-bounded heavy-work scheduler.

active-gate-authoritative-repair-backoff.description: Failed authoritative-repair backoff must remain non-bypassable while newer evidence or retry ownership can still re-drive the single startup ACTIVE decision owner.

admin-notification-repair-cache-owner-ha.description: Admin notification lifecycle transitions and cache-bound snapshot/repair state must observe the same cache owner generation, so shutdown cannot rebind delivery and an old repair completion or deferral cannot govern a replacement cache.

operation-ledger-self-move-hold-dispatch.description: The coordinator's hold registration/admission lanes and the workflow owner's self-move dispatch claim must keep agreeing on who holds the ledger self-move interlock: an engagement that refuses on a remembered holder without reading its row starves every re-planned self-move behind a terminal predecessor.

formation-release-seed-contract-joiner-c.description: The seed release authority and the joiner consumer/barrier must keep agreeing on a retained cohort generation: a consumer predicate that nulls a valid seed contract strands the cohort on the raw spread predicate (the 2026-08-28..30 class), so any change to either endpoint re-runs both formation-release witnesses.

sql-engine-cache-membership.description: The SQL engine and the system-table cache agree on membership rows: what the CDC owner writes, the engine reads back. Seamed in the membership-consistency harness, real in the seven-node probe.

raft-rs-runtime-lifecycle-entry.description: Lifecycle admission and core entry must remain one boundary: retirement cannot race an admitted operation, and queued ingress must recheck lifecycle before worker-side core entry.

raft-rs-runtime-application-transaction.description: The Ready owner and application transaction owner must agree on the durable point from which recovery may replay without duplicating application effects or splitting applied progress from ConfState.

partition-raft-operation-port.description: The raft-rs operation-port owner and the PartitionService consumer must agree on the exact frozen semantic port and its typed outcomes, with no node/control fallback and no second consensus runtime on either side.

spread-cure-transition-authorization.description: The mint and the receiving guard must agree on one authorization record: what the policy owner states, the learner decodes, evaluates and logs.

partition-session-transaction-store-pers.description: The transaction owner ends a user session before proposing its marker exactly when the rs-raft store's persistence admission would refuse a consensus write inside that session.

partition-write-answer-retry-classificat.description: The write-answer owners and the consumers that retry or re-send a write must agree on one classification of each answer: its code and its text say the same, but for the unknown outcome, which only a caller carrying its entryId routes again.

committed-bootstrap-stamp.description: The leader-read producer and target/raft consumer must agree on one canonical committed bootstrap stamp, including its fail-closed transport and shape boundary.

replace-owner-membership-observation.description: A change to how a replica announces, relays or answers its configuration, leader or term must keep the REPLACE owner's wakes, majority-current leader authority, completion and named handoff correct; a change to the owner must keep using only decoded consensus observations.

public-binding-table-policy-merge-decisi.description: The table-policy mutation owner and live split/merge decision owner must agree that the public Binding harness's nonvacuous split children are merge-ineligible before exact one-child versus two-child routing is proved.

partition-replication-record-physical-st.description: The durable workflow record must accept the exact attempt, fence, and payload before one PartitionService worker begins; transport acknowledgement without handler processing cannot bridge the two owners.

storage-reservation-operation-and-retry-.description: The reservation owner may adopt an operation-derived hold only when the replica_operations owner proves the exact immutable generation is still non-terminal. Insertion and authoritative reconciliation consume the operation mutation owner single existing retry deadline; temporary operation-authority loss retains the exact hold and redrives only through the canonical transition and dispatch gate, including after restart.
